account:
Today my official business is the mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at the east-bank cottage at fifteen, office hours at sixteen thirty, and an approved great hall lighting inspection at eighteen. I am still in the office at ten, so I need to leave for the mill promptly.

The unusual feature is how much attention people are giving the evening lighting inspection. The secretary's addendum says the builder and I will inspect eight installed lanterns and the lighting around four tables. The innkeeper originally sought an eighteen hundred meeting, but now says his only business is confirming that inspection. He wants the secretary, builder and himself to meet me here at seventeen thirty and accompany me into the hall at eighteen. The builder is waiting nearby. This could simply be coordination for the inspection, but the innkeeper's involvement and insistence on assembling beforehand make me wonder whether there is some additional gathering or arrangement I have not been told about. I have no direct evidence of its purpose beyond the stated inspection.

There has also been confusion over office records. A provisional appointment book differed from the original; the secretary explained it was not a replacement, and I have verified the original schedule and approved addendum. The identity and whereabouts of the town accounts ledger remain unclear to me, and the innkeeper says he does not know its last handler. The secretary has also asked whom to approach for today's council letters. I have requested factual inquiries and a correspondence check rather than guessing where records are kept.

My neighbour has confirmed tea at fifteen at the cottage. I overheard only a fragment about a bridge or port change at the bakery, without enough context to understand it. The baker is advertising bread at the ordinary price of one emerald. Those scraps do not establish a connection to the hall arrangements. For now, my suspicion of something happening without me remains a suspicion, not a known plot.
